To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the infrared fixed point of QCD and dark-QCD gauge couplings can be used to dynamically relate the QCD and dark matter scales; (2) this mechanism can explain the similarity of dark and visible matter energy densities, as well as the similarity of proton and dark baryon masses; and (3) the mechanism can be tested by direct detection and collider experiments.

the dark matter mass and the dark matter density are naturally comparable to ordinary matter, and the dark matter mass is predicted to be at the electroweak scale, which can be tested at the LHC and at direct detection experiments.

the similarity of dark and ordinary matter energy density is naturally explained by infrared fixed points of QCD and dark-QCD gauge couplings, and that the mass of dark baryons is predicted to be comparable to the mass of ordinary baryons, which can be tested by dark matter direct detection experiments and novel collider signatures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a dynamical mechanism to explain the similarity of dark and ordinary matter energy density.
the question of why the mass scales of ordinary matter and dark matter are similar.
a new class of theories of dark matter that are inspired by the successes of the Standard Model of particle physics and its strong interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dark matter mass is about 1 TeV, and the dark QCD scale is about 10 GeV.
dark matter is ordinary matter in disguise.

a dark QCD with a confinement scale comparable to our QCD confinement scale, together with a dark matter baryogenesis mechanism, can naturally explain the similarity between the dark and ordinary matter energy density in the Universe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dark matter mass and its energy density, the proton mass, and the baryon asymmetry in our Universe can be naturally related to each other through the infrared dynamics of dark QCD and QCD.

the similarity of dark baryons and ordinary baryons, dark matter and ordinary baryonic matter, and the dark matter energy density and ordinary baryogenic matter energy density are naturally explained by dark QCD, which is a new strong interaction that confines at the same energy scale as ordinary QCD.
dark QCD, together with the dark matter baryon asymmetry mechanism, is an attractive framework to explain the origin of dark matter, dark matter mass scale, and dark matter relic density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dark matter and dark baryons could be as massive as the proton, and that the dark sector could be probed at the LHC.
the dark sector could be a mirror image of the ordinary sector.
the mass scales of dark matter, ordinary matter and the Higgs boson can be dynamically related to each other.
